topic_name: A Percentage Is a Fraction in Disguise
title: Out of Every Hundred
description: Under a header reading "Out of Every Hundred", four panels appear side by side. The first panel shows a 10 by 10 grid of 100 squares with 25 shaded amber, captioned "25%". The second shows "₹100" pointing to 100 coins in 10 rows of 10, with 25 amber coins and 75 grey coins, labelled "25/100". The third shows a circle cut into four equal quarters with one quarter shaded amber, labelled "1/4" and captioned "25% = 25/100 = 1/4". The fourth panel displays 40 children in 4 rows of 10, highlighting the top 10, captioned "10 out of 40" and "Also 25%". Two green tags below read "per cent = per centum"...

title: Three Quarters Is 75 Out of 100
description: A horizontal bar is divided into 4 equal cells, with the first 3 cells shaded light blue and the fourth cell unshaded with a grey border. topic_name: Using Percentages to Compare and to Measure Change
title: Same-Size Bars for Two Drink Mixes
labels: Different pack sizes (150 g and 400 g), same bar length: that is what percentages do.
description: A heading reads "Same-Size Bars for Two Drink Mixes" above "Different pack sizes (150 g and 400 g), same bar length: that is what percentages do." Two equal-length horizontal bars represent "DEF" at "150 g" and "Zacni" at "400 g". Each bar has four coloured segments: DEF has brown "66%", cream "20%", green "8%", and grey "6%"; Zacni has brown "68%", cream "16%", green "10%", and grey "6%". Arrows link callouts reading "66% and 68% sugar", "Badam: 8% vs 10%", and "Food chemicals: 6% vs 6%, equal!". Below sits a legend for "Sugar", "Milk solids", "Badam", and "Food chemicals".
